title: Hilbert 14: Optimal Degree Bounds for the Symmetric Group Sₙ
description: The parent (hilbert-14) asks (OQ-02) for the optimal degree bound on generators of invariant rings of reductive groups — hard in general. This entry settles it completely for the fundamental example, the symmetric group Sₙ acting by permuting variables: by the Fundamental Theorem of Symmetric Polynomials, R[x₁,…,xₙ]^{Sₙ} is freely generated by the n elementary symmetric polynomials e₁,…,eₙ, with eₖ homogeneous of degree k, so the optimal bound is β(Sₙ) = n. We package Mathlib's Fundamental Theorem (esymmAlgHom_surjective, esymmAlgEquiv) in invariant-theory language, prove the generators are algebraically independent (optimal number), and prove each eₖ is homogeneous of degree k (optimal degree), all 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext:
Hilbert's 14th problem asks whether the ring of invariants R[V]^G of a group G acting on a polynomial ring is always finitely generated. Hilbert proved this for reductive groups (his celebrated finiteness theorem and basis theorem); Nagata gave a non-reductive counterexample. A natural refinement, raised here as the parent's OQ-02, asks for the OPTIMAL degree bound: the smallest D such that R[V]^G is generated by invariants of degree ≤ D. For finite groups, Noether's bound gives D ≤ |G|, and Noether's degree bound is sharp in general; for reductive groups the sharp constants are subtle and an active research topic.

The cleanest, completely solved instance is the symmetric group Sₙ acting on R[x₁,…,xₙ] by permuting the variables. Its invariant ring is exactly the algebra of symmetric polynomials, and the Fundamental Theorem of Symmetric Polynomials (Newton, Gauss) states that this algebra is freely generated by the n elementary symmetric polynomials e₁,…,eₙ, with eₖ homogeneous of degree k. Therefore the optimal degree bound is β(Sₙ) = n, attained by eₙ = x₁⋯xₙ, and the number of generators is exactly n (they are algebraically independent). Mathlib formalizes the Fundamental Theorem (esymmAlgHom_surjective and the iso esymmAlgEquiv); this entry packages it as the optimal-bound answer for Sₙ and supplies the degree facts.
overview.problemStatement: For the symmetric group Sₙ acting on R[x₁,…,xₙ], determine the optimal degree bound on generators of the invariant ring R[x₁,…,xₙ]^{Sₙ}. Prove: (1) the invariants are generated by e₁,…,eₙ; (2) these n generators are algebraically independent (optimal number); (3) eₖ is homogeneous of degree k, so the generators have degrees 1,…,n and β(Sₙ) = n.
overview.proofStrategy: Generation is Mathlib's esymmAlgHom_surjective: the algebra map MvPolynomial (Fin n) R → symmetricSubalgebra sending Xᵢ ↦ eᵢ₊₁ is surjective, so every symmetric polynomial is aeval (e₁,…,eₙ) of some polynomial. Optimal number: esymmAlgHom is also injective (esymmAlgHom_injective), and factoring aeval through the subalgebra inclusion (injective) gives that the generators are algebraically independent via algebraicIndependent_iff_injective_aeval. Degrees: from esymm_eq_sum_monomial, eₖ is a sum of monomials of multidegree the indicator of a k-subset; that indicator has Finsupp.degree equal to the subset cardinality k, so each monomial — and hence eₖ — is homogeneous of degree k (isHomogeneous_monomial + IsHomogeneous.sum). totalDegree ≤ n follows for all n generators.
keyInsights: For the symmetric group the optimal degree bound is exactly known and small: β(Sₙ) = n, with generators e₁,…,eₙ of degrees 1,…,n.
The bound is sharp on both counts: there are exactly n generators (algebraically independent, by the Fundamental Theorem isomorphism), and the top generator eₙ = x₁⋯xₙ genuinely has degree n.

Mathlib's Fundamental Theorem of Symmetric Polynomials (esymmAlgHom_surjective + esymmAlgEquiv) is precisely the optimal-generation statement; the remaining work is the degree computation eₖ.IsHomogeneous k.
The degree of eₖ reduces to a combinatorial fact: the multidegree of a squarefree monomial over a k-subset is the indicator finsupp, whose Finsupp.degree (a sum) equals the subset cardinality k.
Sₙ is the model case for Hilbert 14: finite (hence reductive), invariants finitely generated, and the optimal bound exactly computable — a concrete anchor for the parent's general open question.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 100 lines and 5 theorems resolving the parent's OQ-02 (optimal degree bound on invariant-ring generators) for the symmetric group Sₙ: the invariants are generated by the n algebraically-independent elementary symmetric polynomials e₁,…,eₙ, with eₖ homogeneous of degree k, so β(Sₙ) = n. Built on Mathlib's Fundamental Theorem of Symmetric Polynomials, with the degree computations proved here.
conclusion.implications: This pins down the optimal degree bound exactly for the model reductive group of invariant theory. It exhibits the sharp answer on both axes — n algebraically independent generators of degrees 1,…,n — and so serves as the concrete anchor case for the parent's general open question about reductive groups. The degree-computation lemma (eₖ.IsHomogeneous k) is a reusable fact about elementary symmetric polynomials that Mathlib did not previously expose. The general reductive case (sharp Noether-type bounds beyond Sₙ) remains open.
openQuestions: Formalize Noether's degree bound β(G) ≤ |G| for an arbitrary finite group G acting linearly (characteristic 0), generalizing the Sₙ result to all finite — hence reductive — groups.
Identify the optimal bound for other classical reductive groups (e.g. SLₙ or GLₙ acting on forms) and formalize the corresponding generating invariants and their degrees.
